info.text: Unit 16 assessment — dispatch decision under pressure. Learners listen again to the dialogues, read short maintenance-documentation texts, apply reported speech, and match dispatch-control vocabulary.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. What defect did the crew write up in the technical log?

generalfeedback.text: Anna reports that "the centre-tank fuel indication read zero" and that the indication is inoperative. The other faults belong to different scenarios in the unit.

answer.text: The centre-tank fuel indication read zero.

feedback.text: Correct — the fuel-quantity indication for the centre tank is inoperative.

answer.text: The left main-gear brake temperature reading was too high.

feedback.text: No — that is the situation used in the writing task, not Dialogue 1.

answer.text: The number-two VHF radio was intermittent.

feedback.text: No — no radio fault is mentioned in Dialogue 1.

answer.text: The green hydraulic pump lost pressure.

feedback.text: No — that is the situation on role-play card 1, not Dialogue 1.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. What did the records office say about the airworthiness directive inspection?

generalfeedback.text: Mark reports the records office said "the repetitive inspection had been done on Monday" — note the backshift to the past perfect when the words are relayed.

answer.text: The repetitive inspection had been done on Monday.

feedback.text: Correct — the check was already complete, so the aircraft was in compliance.

answer.text: The repetitive inspection had been cancelled by the authority.

feedback.text: No — the inspection was done, not cancelled.
No — the directive was still valid.

answer.text: The inspection was overdue by a week.

feedback.text: No — nothing was overdue; the next threshold was still ahead.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Mark said the minimum equipment list added a restriction: the centre tank must stay empty.

generalfeedback.text: True. The MEL allows the deferral but adds a restriction — the centre tank stays empty for this dispatch.

feedback.text: Correct — the restriction is stated clearly at the end of Dialogue 1.
Listen again — Mark says the centre tank must stay empty.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. The captain refused to accept the aircraft with the restriction.

generalfeedback.text: False. The captain says, "I am happy to accept the aircraft with that restriction." She accepts, she does not refuse.

feedback.text: Correct — the captain accepts the aircraft.
No — she was happy to accept the aircraft with the restriction.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. How many days is the rectification interval for this category C item? Write the number of days.

generalfeedback.text: The interval is ten calendar days — a category C item under the minimum equipment list.

feedback.text: Correct — ten calendar days.
Listen again — the interval is ten days.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. For how many flight hours is the next inspection threshold not yet due? Write the number of hours.

generalfeedback.text: Mark says the next threshold was "not due for forty flight hours", so the aircraft is inside the interval and in compliance.

feedback.text: Correct — forty flight hours remain before the next threshold.
Listen again — the figure is forty flight hours.

questiontext.text:
Read the work order, then answer.

WORK ORDER 4471 — A320 YL-BBX. Task: replace the number-two VHF transceiver. The BITE test passed after fitment. The technician recorded the part numbers and signed the stage. A duplicate inspection was raised for the antenna cable.

What did the technician do after the BITE test passed?

generalfeedback.text: The order states the technician "recorded the part numbers and signed the stage" once the built-in test equipment (BITE) test passed.

answer.text: Recorded the part numbers and signed the stage.

feedback.text: Correct — that is the action written in the work order.

answer.text: Removed the transceiver again and ordered a new antenna cable.

feedback.text: No — the cable had a duplicate inspection, not a replacement.

answer.text: Deferred the task under the minimum equipment list.

feedback.text: No — the task was completed, not deferred.

answer.text: Left the stage open for the next shift.

feedback.text: No — the technician signed the stage.

questiontext.text:
Read the note, then answer.

An MEL item may carry a maintenance procedure marked (M) and an operational procedure marked (O). The (M) procedure is the engineer's job; the (O) procedure is the flight crew's job.

Statement: the (O) procedure is carried out by the maintenance staff.

generalfeedback.text: False. The (O) procedure is the flight crew's job; the (M) procedure is the engineer's job.

feedback.text: Correct — (O) is operational, done by the crew.
No — read again: (O) is the flight crew's job.

questiontext.text:
Read the service bulletin, then answer.

SERVICE BULLETIN A320-28-1234. The manufacturer recommends a fuel-pump wiring modification. Compliance is optional unless an airworthiness directive makes the bulletin mandatory.

When does this service bulletin become mandatory?

generalfeedback.text: A service bulletin (SB) is a recommendation. It becomes mandatory only when an airworthiness directive adopts it.

answer.text: When an airworthiness directive makes it mandatory.

feedback.text: Correct — an AD can turn a recommended SB into a required action.

answer.text: As soon as the manufacturer issues the bulletin to the operator.

feedback.text: No — issuing the SB does not make it mandatory on its own.
No — the interval belongs to deferred defects, not to the SB.

answer.text: After the next repetitive inspection is signed.

feedback.text: No — the SB status does not depend on the inspection.

questiontext.text:
Read the BITE readout, then answer.

BITE READOUT — FUEL QUANTITY. Fault code 28-41 stored. The signal from the centre-tank probe is open circuit. The fault is confirmed, not intermittent.

Statement: the centre-tank probe fault is intermittent.

generalfeedback.text: False. The readout says the fault is "confirmed, not intermittent" — it is a steady open circuit.

feedback.text: Correct — the fault is confirmed and steady.
No — the readout states it is not intermittent.

name.text: U16-U1 Reported speech · present to past

questiontext.text:
Report the words. Write ONE word in the gap.

Direct: "The item is deferred." → The planner said the item ______ deferred.

generalfeedback.text: The backshift moves is to was when you relay the words.

feedback.text: Correct — is → was.
Backshift is needed here: is → was.

name.text: U16-U2 Reported speech · can to could

questiontext.text:
Report the words. Write ONE word in the gap.

Direct: "We can dispatch." → She said we ______ dispatch.

generalfeedback.text: The modal can steps back to could.

feedback.text: Correct — can → could.
Backshift the modal: can → could.

name.text: U16-U3 Reported speech · must to had to

questiontext.text:
Report the words. Write TWO words in the gap.

Direct: "The tank must stay empty." → He said the tank ______ stay empty.

generalfeedback.text: Must becomes had to in reported speech.

feedback.text: Correct — must → had to.
Change the modal: must → had to.

questiontext.text:
Report the question. Write ONE word in the gap.

Direct: "Is the inspection valid?" → She asked ______ the inspection was valid.

generalfeedback.text: A yes/no question is reported with whether (or if), and the word order becomes a statement.

feedback.text: Correct — "asked whether the inspection was valid".
Also correct — "if" works here too.
No — use "whether" or "if" for a yes/no question.

questiontext.text:
Choose the right verb. Write ONE word in the gap.

He ______ me the centre tank was empty. (use the verb that takes a person)

generalfeedback.text: Use tell with a person (tell me), and say with no person after it.

feedback.text: Correct — "told me". "Tell" takes a person.
No — "said me" is wrong; use "told me".

questiontext.text:
Write the missing term.

The time limit to repair a deferred item is the ______ interval.

generalfeedback.text: The rectification interval is the repair time limit set by the item's repair category.

feedback.text: Correct — the rectification interval.
Close — the noun form is "rectification".

questiontext.text: Match each dispatch-control term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: These five terms carry the unit: deferral, restriction, proviso, placard and threshold.

answer.text: putting off a repair to a later time
a limit on how the aircraft may be operated
a condition you must meet to dispatch
a warning label near a broken control
the point when an action becomes due
the departure window given by air traffic control

questiontext.text: Match each verb to the noun it goes with in dispatch English.

generalfeedback.text: Word partners matter: hold the slot, raise a deferred defect, sign the certificate, fit a placard.

questiontext.text: Which word means "the ground time to prepare the aircraft between flights"?

generalfeedback.text: The turnaround is the ground time between two flights. The slot is the departure window; the threshold is a due point; the interval is a repair time limit.

feedback.text: Correct — the ground time between flights.

answer.text: the departure slot from air traffic control

feedback.text: No — that is the slot, the departure window.
No — the interval is a repair time limit.

answer.text: the threshold of the next inspection

feedback.text: No — the threshold is the due point of an action.

questiontext.text: Complete the collocation from the tech log: "______ a deferred defect."

generalfeedback.text: You raise a deferred defect in the technical log. The other verbs collocate with different nouns.

feedback.text: Correct — raise a deferred defect.
No — you confirm the fuel, not the deferred defect.
No — an interval expires; you do not expire a defect.
No — you placard a control, not a defect.
